cover.headline: Agency 2026 Brand Guide
cover.subtitle: Colour, type, marks, circuit art, media, writing, motion and sound for every Agency 2026 piece.

pages.title: How to Use This Guide
pages.lead: Agency 2026 runs **December 7 to 9, 2026, in Edmonton and Calgary**. Every handout, slide, banner, film and stage graphic for the event uses one look: the circuit-board art of the invite, navy type, a red date line and a spectrum of accent colours.

head: You need
Look in
rows: brand/fonts (Inter, Geist Mono) and Arial for Office files
Templates for print, slides, digital and Office

items: Use only the facts you were given. Label every example value as an example.
Take every colour, font and size from the tokens. Never pick a colour by eye.
Check every piece before it ships: the fit check, the writing lint, the QR check, and a look at the output.

blocks.title: Open decision: two palettes
blocks.text: The MVAI video kit uses **Inter** and navy #022C4C. The event team's slide template, motion library and invites use **Arial or Liberation Sans** and navy #002C4E. The owner decides which set is canonical. Until then, keep each piece in one set.

pages.title: Colour
pages.lead: Navy carries the type. Red marks the date. The spectrum colours mark sections, charts and art. Each section of a piece takes one accent.

blocks.text: The first value is the fill colour, for bars, rules, tiles and traces. The text value is the darker shade that reaches 4.5 to 1 contrast on white. Use it for words.

blocks.title: The Two Palettes Side by Side

head: Role
MVAI kit
Event team
rows: slide template, motion library, invites, Office files

items: **Board** (white) is the default for every medium.
**Night** and **navy** give contrast on a few slides or scenes per piece.
**Spectrum** is for the one line people should remember, once per piece.

pages.title: Type and Marks
pages.lead: Inter carries every headline and paragraph in HTML, PDF and video. Geist Mono sets kickers, labels and the classification pill. Office files use Arial.

items: **Agency 2026 wordmark:** Agency in navy, 2026 in red, over the trace underline: one thin blue trace that steps down and ends in a ring pad. It sits top-left on every page, slide and frame. Use the outlined SVG where the font may be missing.
**Alberta signature:** top-right on content pages, bottom-right on covers and end cards. Use the supplied files only. Keep clear space of at least the height of its blue square on every side.
**Never** recolour, stretch, outline, crop or redraw the signature.
**Bird mark:** a stock vector with no confirmed licence. Do not use it until the licence is recorded.

cols.text: Clear space: keep the height of the blue square free on every side of the signature.

pages.title: Circuit Art and Layout
pages.lead: The trace art is the signature of the event. It belongs on covers, title cards, section cards, end cards and one-message pieces. Content pages stay a clean board.

items: Traces run in from the edges, bend only at 45 degrees and end in white ring pads.
Left edge purple, blue and cyan. Top lilac, pink and orange. Right yellow, lime and green.
Corners stay clear. Art never sits behind text, charts or tables.
Make new arrangements with scripts/vectors.mjs and a seed. Record the seed with the piece.
The pink microchip appears once per piece, on the splash, cover or title card.

cols.alt: The Agency 2026 invite: circuit traces around the event title

cols.text: Generated frame: node scripts/vectors.mjs traces --seed frame-16x9

blocks.text: Every page, slide and frame ends in a navy band with the classification on the right. The default is UNCLASSIFIED. The content owner sets the level; nobody infers it from the material.

pages.title: Which Template for Which Piece
pages.lead: Pick the template, copy its sample content file, and replace the content. The template owns the design.

head: Piece
Template or tool
Output
rows: Poster, agenda, certificate, badge, table tent, demo card, postcard
Briefing note, memo, speaker brief, event report
Social post, story, web banner, Teams background, signage
Stage openers, bumpers, lower thirds, countdowns
The full event day on one laptop

items: Office files use Arial, so they look the same on every government computer.
Word templates have styles for Title, Heading 1 to 3, Kicker, Callout, Note and tables. Use the styles; do not format by hand.
The PowerPoint template has 13 layouts, from the title and day sections to two columns, four stats and the agenda.

pages.title: QR Codes and Accessibility
pages.lead: Every piece must work for every reader. Every QR code must scan on the first try.

items: Dark modules on a light ground, with a quiet zone of four modules.
At least 2 cm wide when printed, larger for signs read from a distance.
Use short official https addresses. Show the address in text beside the code.
A centre badge forces the highest error correction.
Run scripts/qr-verify.mjs, then scan the printed proof with a phone.
Text reaches 4.5 to 1 contrast, or 3 to 1 for large type. Use the text-safe accent shades.
Never carry meaning by colour alone. Label every bar, line and tile.
Every picture has alt text. Decorative art is marked as decorative.
Use real headings in order. Tables have a header row.
Videos have captions. Narration describes what the screen shows.

blocks.text: A passing check does not prove a page looks right. Look at every page before it ships.

pages.title: Writing
pages.lead: Write in plain declarative language. Make a claim, give its source, and move on.

items: One idea per sentence, mostly under 20 words.
Lead with the plain point, then explain it.
Explain each technical term the first time it appears.
Name who does what.
Headings are plain labels with no end punctuation.
Say **AI agent** for the AI. Staff are also called agents.
Every figure has a source in a NOTES file.
The contrast shape that denies one thing to assert another
Slogans, taglines and closing flourishes nobody supplied
Lists of more than three items inside a sentence
Announcing what a page or film will do
Softeners such as simply, just and really
Invented names, numbers, dates or quotes

blocks.text: Run python3 scripts/lint/lint.py on every content file. Fix every error. A person decides on each warning. Conclusions, lessons, asks and closing lines come from the content owner.

pages.title: Motion and Sound
pages.lead: Motion and music make the day feel like one show. The same motion grammar and one sonic palette run from the walk-in to the close.

items: Traces draw themselves on; signals pulse along them.
Type rises into place on the spoken word. Text never scales while it moves.
Scenes change with a fast bus sweep of coloured traces, about half a second.
Stage pieces: opening titles, day bumpers, speaker lower third, session countdown, stat reveal, logo sting.
Render with scripts/motion-render.mjs and look at the stills.
One palette: cinematic electronic with organic percussion, bright plucks, warm bass.
Tempo 92 to 104 bpm. D major for openers and triumph.
A rising three-note pluck opens every sting and bumper.
Every cue is mastered to -16 LUFS and fades cleanly.
The cue list and Suno prompts are in guides/SOUND.md.

blocks.text: The show player runs the whole event day from one laptop: countdowns to the next session, speaker welcomes, slides, videos with sound and music between transitions. The control booth steps forward and back through the agenda. See guides/SHOW.md.

pages.title: Do and Do Not
pages.lead: Most problems come from a colour picked by eye, art behind text or a number nobody supplied.

head: Do
Do not
rows: Pick colours by eye or from a screenshot
Use the text-safe shade for words
Set yellow, lime or cyan text on white
Keep content pages and slides clean
Put traces behind charts, tables or paragraphs
Use every spectrum colour on one slide
Use the spectrum ground once per piece
Make a spectrum slide for every point
Use the bundled fonts, or Arial in Office
Use the supplied Alberta signature files
Recolour, crop or redraw the signature
Use red as a general accent
Show the classification on every page
Remove the band to gain space
Test every QR code with a phone
Print a code nobody has scanned
